change.title: ao-replay/8720-r2
change.description: fix(spawn): share one deadline across base resolution and fetch
change.author: ronish

findings.title: New test passes without the shared-budget change
findings.body: `TestRefreshDefaultBranchesSharesOneBudgetAcrossResolution` cannot fail on the regression it names, for two reasons. (1) `resolveRemoteFunc` is only called from `fakeWorkspace.ResolveDefaultBranchWithin` (line 1319). If the manager went back to calling `refresher.ResolveDefaultBranch` for each repo, the fake's plain `ResolveDefaultBranch` (line 1303) never reads `resolveRemoteFunc` and returns at once, so the test passes. (2) The 250ms limit does not tell a shared deadline from a per-repo one. With a 25ms timeout, four repos that each waited their own 25ms would take about 100ms, still under 250ms. The sibling `TestRefreshDefaultBranchesUsesOneOverallFetchBudget` (line 6025) has the same loose limit. Make the test measure the sharing: use a larger budget (for example 200ms, so four serial waits come to 800ms) and assert a tight upper bound. Better, have `resolveRemoteFunc` record `remoteCtx.Deadline()` for each call and assert all four deadlines are equal. A check on `len(baseRefs)` alone also passes in both cases.

findings.title: One stalled repo makes later repos fail resolution instead of getting their own lookup
findings.body: Resolution now shares `fetchCtx` with the fetches. `resolveAutomaticDefault` (workspace.go:2058) answers from Git's cached HEAD when one exists, so only repos with no cached `origin/HEAD` reach `resolver.Resolve`. For those, the live lookup runs on `remoteCtx` (gitdefault/resolver.go:151). If an earlier repo's lookup uses the whole 5s, every later uncached repo starts with an expired `remoteCtx`. `Resolve` then falls to `cachedRemoteHead` and `initializedBeforeFirstPush` (resolver.go:178-187), and with neither it returns an unresolved error. The manager logs a warning and leaves `targets[i].resolved` empty. That repo gets no `baseRefs` entry and no fetch (line 2267). Before this change each repo got its own 5s lookup. This is the intended trade for bounding total latency, but it makes a worker's base-ref choice for children depend on the order of the repo list. Say so in the PR body, or decide whether a small per-repo floor is wanted.

findings.title: No test for router delegation of ResolveDefaultBranchWithin
findings.body: The router has a new delegation method with a fallback branch (lines 64-67). `router_test.go` only covers `ResolveDefaultBranch` through `recordingWorkspace`. The production path goes through this router, so a test that the budgeted method reaches the git adapter, and that the fallback is used when the adapter lacks the interface, would protect the `remoteCtx` plumbing.

contracts.action: Default-branch resolution during spawn now runs on the shared refresh deadline (fetchCtx) instead of a per-repo 5s budget
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this change, gitworktree.ResolveDefaultBranch created its own defaultBranchResolutionBudget (5s) for each repo. The manager then ran a separate shared fetchCtx (defaultBranchRefreshTimeout, 5s) over the fetches. worktree-creation callers still use resolveWorktreeRefsWithBudget (workspace.go:2124).
contracts.before_after: Before: worst case about N×5s of resolution plus 5s of fetch. After: one 5s deadline covers resolution and fetch together. ResolveDefaultBranch is kept as a wrapper that builds its own budget (workspace.go:192-196), so other callers behave as before. The router forwards to the git adapter and falls back to ResolveDefaultBranch when the adapter lacks the interface (router.go:63-68). The manager falls back the same way when the workspace does not implement the budgeted interface (manager.go:2237-2242).
contracts.visible_effect: Spawn latency is bounded by one defaultBranchRefreshTimeout for the whole refresh. Local reads (Inspect, refExists) use ctx and keep working after the deadline. Repos needing a live lookup after the budget is spent fail resolution and go without base ref or fetch (see finding at manager.go:2235). Resolution that succeeds live consumes budget the later fetches need.
contracts.failure_mode: If remoteCtx expires, Resolve falls back to the cached HEAD or the AO-initialized branch, otherwise it returns an error. The manager logs a warning and continues with the adapter fallback (manager.go:2252-2258), so the spawn proceeds and the failure is visible only in logs. Nothing persists beyond this call. The background HEAD refresh uses its own context (workspace.go:2086).

summary: The change correctly shares one deadline across default-branch resolution and fetch, with a safe fallback when an adapter lacks the new interface. The new test cannot catch a regression, because it passes whether or not the manager uses the budgeted method and its 250ms limit cannot tell a shared deadline from per-repo ones. One tradeoff to note: a repo whose live lookup stalls leaves later uncached repos with no base ref. The router's new delegation has no test.
